title: Tangent and existence criterion for a functor of ring deformations
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathrm{Art}_k$ be the category of Artinian local commutative $k$-algebras with specified residue field $k$, and local $k$-maps respecting it; Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize. For any commutative $k$-algebra $B$, let $\mathrm{Def}_B(A)$ be the groupoid of flat $A$-algebras $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] with a specified quotient $Q/\mathfrak m_AQ\cong B$, with isomorphisms respecting the quotient and with algebra base change between the groupoids. Its tangent space $T_B$ is the set of isomorphism classes in $\mathrm{Def}_B(k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$. It is naturally the $k$-vector space $\operatorname{Exal}_k(B,B)$: the latter means square-zero $k$-algebra extensions $0\to B\to E\to B\to0$, with the prescribed kernel module structure, modulo isomorphisms that are identity on kernel and quotient, equipped with Baer sum and scalar multiplication. The identification sends a flat dual-number deformation to the extension with kernel map $b\mapsto\epsilon\widetilde b$. Let $B,C$ be commutative $k$-algebras and $F:\mathrm{Def}_B\to\mathrm{Def}_C$ a functor commuting with base change. Its tangent map is $k$-linear. Suppose that (i) $T_B\to T_C$ is surjective, and (ii) for every surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ in $\mathrm{Art}_k$ whose kernel $I$ has $\dim_k I=1$ and $\mathfrak m_{A'}I=0$, and every $Q\in\mathrm{Def}_B(A)$, existence of a marked flat lift of $F(Q)$ over $A'$ implies existence of a marked flat lift of $Q$. Then $F$ is smooth in the marked sense: for any surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, any $Q\in\mathrm{Def}_B(A)$, and any $D\in\mathrm{Def}_C(A')$ with a specified isomorphism $D\otimes_{A'}A\cong F(Q)$, there is $Q'\in\mathrm{Def}_B(A')$ and isomorphisms $Q'\otimes_{A'}A\cong Q$ and $F(Q')\cong D$ inducing the specified isomorphism over $A$.

proof.text: Use $R=k$ in the Artinian test category; a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,k$, and it is finite type over itself. For $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ with $A_2\to A$ surjective, flat algebras $Q_1,Q_2$ and a reduction isomorphism give the algebra $E=Q_1\times_{Q_2\otimes_{A_2}A}Q_2$. The flat-presentation node makes $E$ flat over $A_1\times_A A_2$. The patched-module node gives its two canonical base-change isomorphisms; these are algebra isomorphisms since their maps preserve multiplication. Conversely the flat-presentation node reconstructs any flat algebra from its two base changes. Maps between the pairs induce maps of fibre products by $(q_1,q_2)\mapsto(u_1q_1,u_2q_2)$, and the reconstruction is natural, so these constructions are inverse on arrows as well as objects. They preserve the specified special-fibre identifications. The base fibre $\mathrm{Def}_B(k)$ has a unique arrow between any two marked objects, so $\mathrm{Def}_B$, and likewise $\mathrm{Def}_C$, are predeformation categories satisfying (RS).

Write $D=k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. For a flat marked $D$-algebra $Q$, tensor $0\to(\epsilon)\to D\to k\to0$ with $Q$. Flat tensor exactness and the quotient-tensor identification give $0\to B\xrightarrow{i}Q\to B\to0$, with $i(b)=\epsilon\widetilde b$. This is independent of the lift because $\epsilon^2=0$, its kernel is square zero, and multiplication by a lift of $b$ on $i(c)$ is $i(bc)$. Conversely, for a square-zero extension $0\to B\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{p}B\to0$, put $\epsilon=i(1)$ to define its $D$-algebra structure. Then $\epsilon e=i(p(e))$, so $\epsilon E=i(B)$ and $E/\epsilon E=B$. Under $(\epsilon)\otimes_D E\cong E/\epsilon E\cong B$, multiplication is the injection $i$. The quotient is flat over $k$, so the nilpotent-ideal flatness criterion with $J=(\epsilon)$ proves $E$ flat over $D$. The two constructions undo each other and match precisely the isomorphisms fixing kernel and quotient. This proves the asserted bijection with $\operatorname{Exal}_k(B,B)$.

proof.text: By the tangent-tensor node and step 1, $T_B$ has its canonical $k$-vector structure. Its addition first glues $Q_1,Q_2$ over $B$ into $Q_1\times_BQ_2$ over $k\oplus(k\oplus k)$, then changes base along $(a,u,v)\mapsto a+(u+v)\epsilon$. On the square-zero kernel $B\oplus B$ this identifies $(i_1(b),-i_2(b))$ with zero; it is exactly pushout along addition $B\oplus B\to B$, hence Baer sum. Base change along $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$ sends the kernel element $i(b)$ to $i_a(ab)$ and fixes the quotient, hence is coefficient pushout by $a$. The square-zero-extension classification states that these operations are the vector addition and scalar action on extension classes. Thus step 2 is a vector-space identification. A functor commuting with base change preserves these vector operations: applying it to the gluing object gives an object with the same pair of restrictions, uniquely determined up to isomorphism by (RS), and it commutes with the sum and scalar base maps. Consequently $dF$ is $k$-linear, including for $a=0$.

Consider a small extension $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ with kernel $I$, an object $Q$ over $A$, and a marked target lift $(D,\delta)$. Hypothesis (ii) supplies a marked lift $(Q'_0,\alpha_0)$. By step 1 and the marked-lift torsor node, the nonempty sets of source and target marked lift classes have free transitive actions of $T_B\otimes_kI$ and $T_C\otimes_kI$, and their map is equivariant for $dF\otimes1_I$. There is a unique $t$ with $[D,\delta]=F[Q'_0,\alpha_0]+t$. Choose $0\ne e\in I$. Since $\dim_k I=1$, write $t=v\otimes e$; tangent surjectivity gives $u$ with $dF(u)=v$. A representative $(Q',\alpha)$ of $[Q'_0,\alpha_0]+u\otimes e$ therefore maps to $[D,\delta]$. Equality of these marked classes supplies an isomorphism $\beta:F(Q')\cong D$ with $\delta\circ\beta|_A=F(\alpha)$, using the coherent base-change comparison. This gives the specified compatibility, not merely an unmarked isomorphism.

For an arbitrary surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, the Artinian test-algebra node factors it as $A'=A_n\twoheadrightarrow A_{n-1}\twoheadrightarrow\cdots\twoheadrightarrow A_0=A$, each arrow a small extension; an isomorphism is the empty case. Put $D_j=D\otimes_{A'}A_j$. Start with $Q_0=Q$ and $F(Q_0)\cong D_0$ inverse to the given $\delta$. Inductively suppose $Q_{j-1}$ and $\beta_{j-1}:F(Q_{j-1})\cong D_{j-1}$ are chosen. Apply step 4 to the target lift $D_j$, marked by $D_j|_{A_{j-1}}\cong D_{j-1}\xrightarrow{\beta_{j-1}^{-1}}F(Q_{j-1})$. It gives $Q_j$, $\alpha_j:Q_j|_{A_{j-1}}\cong Q_{j-1}$ and $\beta_j:F(Q_j)\cong D_j$ with $\beta_j|_{A_{j-1}}=\beta_{j-1}\circ F(\alpha_j)$. At $j=n$, compose the $\alpha_j$ after base change to $A$. The displayed identities give $\delta\circ\beta_n|_A=F(\alpha)$, as required. For the empty factorization take $Q'=Q\otimes_{A,(A'\to A)^{-1}}A'$ and transport the prescribed isomorphism. This proves marked smoothness for every surjection.
